whatsHappening.background: Sudan’s current war grew out of a failed transition after the 2019 revolution that ended Omar al-Bashir’s dictatorship. Civilian hopes for democratic rule were weakened by military control, then the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces carried out a joint coup in 2021. In April 2023, the two forces turned on each other and launched a war for control of the country.

civilianImpact.experiences: The war has pushed civilians into mass displacement, severe hunger, disease outbreaks, and extreme insecurity. Families have fled Khartoum, Darfur, Kordofan, and other areas while hospitals, schools, markets, and water systems have been damaged or shut down. Reports of atrocities, sexual violence, ethnic targeting, and attacks on health care continue to make daily life dangerous.

whatsHappening.background: Sudan’s war has created a crisis of survival. Food systems have collapsed in many places, famine conditions have appeared in parts of Darfur and Kordofan, and millions have lost access to school, health care, safe water, and protection. Children, displaced families, women and girls, and communities trapped in fighting face the heaviest burden.

civilianImpact.experiences: For civilians, the crisis means fleeing with little warning, searching for food and water, losing access to school and health care, and living under constant insecurity. Humanitarian access is often blocked by fighting, bureaucracy, and attacks, so even areas with extreme need may not receive enough aid.

whatsHappening.background: Helping Sudan means supporting emergency food, health care, water, shelter, and protection for displaced families and communities cut off by war. Local and international relief groups need sustained support because the crisis is underfunded and access remains dangerous.

civilianImpact.experiences: Support should focus on civilian survival: food, health care, protection, water, and shelter. Awareness also matters because Sudan’s crisis is massive but often overlooked, and public pressure can help sustain aid funding and attention on atrocities.
